units.why: The Board-approved change "any academic misconduct concerns to be adjudicated by SCCS where a grade penalty may result", a formal reporting procedure (P81).

units.passage: Even when not considering a grade penalty for academic misconduct violations, we encourage you to utilize the Reporting Academic Misconduct Form to submit incidents for our review.
units.why: Instructors are encouraged to use the reporting form "Even when not considering a grade penalty", a reporting procedure (P81) with should.

units.passage: We can still have educational conversations with students even when there is not enough information to find a violation, so we encourage you to continue to refer these cases to SCCS for review when you have concerns about potential academic misconduct. If you have questions or would otherwise like to discuss the information contained above, please feel free to reach out to me ( diannet@uoregon.edu ) or Linda Gatton ( lgatton@uoregon.edu ) and we can schedule time to connect or correspond by email. Sincerely, Dianne Tanjuaquio, M.Ed.
units.why: "we encourage you to continue to refer these cases to SCCS for review when you have concerns" asks instructors to report suspected misconduct through the central office (P81).

units.passage: suspected use will be referred to the Center for Community Standards & Accountability (CSA)
units.why: "suspected use will be referred to the Center for Community Standards & Accountability" gives the reporting route (P81).

units.passage: b) Gather and preserve any relevant evidence, c) Document the incident and the evidence as soon as possible.
units.why: The faculty member must 'Gather and preserve any relevant evidence' and document the incident. This is a procedural duty (P81); P69 (evidence standards) does not fit as no standard of proof or kind of evidence is named.
units.fit_note: Names evidence gathering and documentation without saying what evidence counts.

units.passage: If the faculty member determines that a violation is likely to have occurred, the faculty member must report the violation to his or her associate dean and supply the relevant documentation, including a short memorandum describing the incident, the evidence and the recommended penalty.
units.why: When a violation is likely, 'the faculty member must report the violation to his or her associate dean' with a memorandum and recommended penalty, a required reporting step (P81).

units.passage: If the violation involved the misuse of AI, the faculty member must provide the associate dean with a copy of the written “Course AI Policy” that the student has violated.
units.why: For AI cases, 'the faculty member must provide the associate dean with a copy of the written "Course AI Policy"'. This is a reporting step (P81) that also presumes instructors have a written course AI policy; P09 does not apply because no duty to write one is stated.
units.fit_note: Implies a written Course AI Policy exists for each course but does not require one.

units.passage: In addition, the faculty member should inform the student that the associate dean will contact them to discuss the alleged violation.
units.why: The faculty member 'should inform the student that the associate dean will contact them to discuss the alleged violation', a procedural notice step in handling a suspected violation (P81).
units.fit_note: Covers notice to the student only; the one-week recommendation is a separate unit.

units.passage: Normally the faculty member is expected to make a recommendation within one week after receiving a report or witnessing an incident.
units.why: The faculty member 'is expected to make a recommendation within one week after receiving a report or witnessing an incident', a deadline in the reporting procedure (P81).
units.fit_note: Deadline for the recommendation only.

units.passage: Throughout the process, the faculty member should preserve the student’s confidentiality to the greatest extent possible and generally not discuss the student's connection with academic dishonesty to anyone other than the associate dean.
units.why: The faculty member 'should preserve the student's confidentiality to the greatest extent possible', a procedural fairness duty in handling cases. P81 is nearest; no type covers confidentiality.
units.fit_note: Concerns confidentiality of the accused student rather than a reporting step.

units.passage: The associate dean will inform the student in writing of the charge and the penalty. The associate dean must maintain a file of all reports.
units.why: The associate dean 'must maintain a file of all reports' and tell the student in writing, a record-keeping and notice procedure (P81).

units.passage: All final decisions and penalties must be conveyed to the student in writing.
units.why: Final decisions 'must be conveyed to the student in writing', a transparency requirement in the process (P81).

units.passage: Violations that result in a grade penalty must be reported to the Provost's Office.
units.why: A procedural duty ('must be reported to the Provost's Office') once a penalty is given, the formal integrity-reporting procedure (P81).

units.passage: Please remember that faculty must file an AIV report if they wish to sanction a student for alleged violations.
units.why: Procedural requirement: 'faculty must file an AIV report' to sanction, the formal reporting procedure (P81).

units.passage: Reports must be submitted within the policy’s timeline so concerns can be addressed promptly.
units.why: 'Reports must be submitted within the policy's timeline' is a procedural reporting duty to SCED (P81).

units.passage: If you determine that an academic integrity violation occurred and impose an academic sanction, you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development (SCED).
units.why: "you must report the matter to Student Conduct and Ethical Development (SCED)" is a mandatory procedural step after imposing a sanction, P81.

units.passage: Under the revised policy, an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting an Academic Integrity Reporting Form
units.why: "an academic sanction may not be imposed without submitting an Academic Integrity Reporting Form" requires a form before sanctioning; distinct from the duty to report, still P81.

units.passage: Consistent reporting allows the university to identify repeat violations, provide appropriate support and interventions, and respond to comparable cases more equitably across campus.
units.why: The reason given, that consistent reporting 'allows the university to identify repeat violations, provide appropriate support', explains the reporting rule; closest type is P81.
units.fit_note: This is a rationale for reporting rather than a procedural step.

units.passage: The report, including supporting documentation and communications with the student, must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident.
units.why: The report 'must be submitted within 15 working days of the incident' is a procedural deadline in the formal reporting process, P81.

units.passage: Establishing clear escalation language, processes, and guidelines in the event of detected plagiarism, at the department level is important.
units.why: 'Establishing clear escalation language, processes, and guidelines ... at the department level is important'; sets up integrity procedure, P81.
units.fit_note: Asks departments to define their own escalation procedure. Asks departments to create escalation procedures, rather than telling instructors to follow a central reporting procedure.

units.passage: Doing so is considered a violation of SCU’s Academic Integrity and suspected use will be reported to the Office of Student Life.
units.why: Sample statement: 'suspected use will be reported to the Office of Student Life'; a reporting step, P81.

units.passage: Doing so is considered a violation of SCU’s Academic Integrity and suspected use will be reported to the Office of Student Life.
units.why: COEN 11 (CSE): 'suspected use will be reported to the Office of Student Life'; reporting step, P81.

units.passage: Follow SCU’s existing protocol to report an academic integrity violation
units.why: Says to 'Follow SCU's existing protocol to report an academic integrity violation'; formal reporting, P81.

units.passage: Faculty and students are directed to use this form when reporting an academic integrity violation.
units.policy: Faculty and students use the form to report an academic integrity violation under SCU's existing protocol.
units.why: 'Faculty and students are directed to use this form when reporting an academic integrity violation'; a required form, P81.

units.passage: In cases where students use generative AI in a way that violates an instructor’s articulated policy, the procedures outlined in Academic Integrity Protocol , as administered by the Office of the Provost and Executive Vice President, will be used to resolve the matter.
units.policy: When students use generative AI in a way that violates an instructor's articulated policy, the Academic Integrity Protocol administered by the Office of the Provost and Executive Vice President is used to resolve the matter.
units.why: Violations of an instructor's policy are resolved by 'the procedures outlined in Academic Integrity Protocol, as administered by the Office of the Provost'; the formal integrity procedure, P81.

units.passage: Following any (discretionary) investigation of a potential academic integrity violation, faculty who have reason to believe that a student has engaged in an academic integrity violation should, within a reasonable amount time (as determined by their Dean’s Designee), notify the student of the allegation by email to the student’s Seattle University email address.
units.policy: Faculty who believe a student has committed an academic integrity violation should notify the student by email, within a reasonable time set by the Dean's Designee.
units.why: Faculty 'may decide, if appropriate, to first investigate a potential academic integrity violation' and then notify the student, which sets the first procedural step for suspected misuse including AI; P81 fits as formal reporting procedure.
units.fit_note: Applies to all academic integrity violations, not only AI.

units.passage: they will determine the appropriate course penalty and complete an Academic Integrity Violation Report form. This form, along with all supporting material, will be promptly forwarded to the Dean’s Designee of the college or school in which the course is offered, the student, and to the chair or program director of the department in which the course is offered, ideally within ten business days of the student-faculty meeting
units.policy: After the meeting, a faculty member who still believes a violation occurred determines the course penalty and completes an Academic Integrity Violation Report form, forwarded to the Dean's Designee, the student and the chair, ideally within ten business days.
units.why: The instructor must 'complete an Academic Integrity Violation Report form' and forward it with supporting material to the Dean's Designee, ideally within ten business days; P81 fits as the formal reporting step.

units.passage: To report a case to the AIB, please use the Academic Integrity Board Reporting Form .
units.why: "To report a case to the AIB, please use the Academic Integrity Board Reporting Form" names the required form, P81.

units.passage: If, after you speak to the student, you still suspect academic dishonesty, inform the student that you are reporting the situation to the Academic Integrity Board.
units.why: "inform the student that you are reporting the situation to the Academic Integrity Board" is a required procedural step, P81.

units.passage: The AIB strongly encourages faculty to submit all cases of suspected violations to the Board.
units.why: 'The AIB strongly encourages faculty to submit all cases of suspected violations to the Board' is the formal reporting step, P81; it is generic to integrity cases on a page that also handles AI cases.

units.passage: Instances of unauthorized GenAI use in coursework will be treated as a violation of the University's Student Academic Conduct Policy and will be processed in the same manner as other academic misconduct violations using the Academic Misconduct Penalty Record (AMPR).
units.why: "processed ... using the Academic Misconduct Penalty Record (AMPR)" names the formal reporting form (P81).

units.passage: Violations involving AI are reviewed under the same process as any other academic integrity case.
units.why: 'Violations involving AI are reviewed under the same process as any other academic integrity case' sets the formal procedure for AI cases, P81.

units.passage: Instructor reporting the concern
units.why: The first step listed is 'Instructor reporting the concern', a procedural duty for instructors in an integrity case, P81.

units.passage: Faculty members who suspect that a student has violated their course AI policy should follow the procedures under the Student’s Code of Conduct policy
units.why: Faculty who suspect violation of the course AI policy "should follow the procedures under the Student’s Code of Conduct policy": a formal procedure, P81.

units.passage: Monitoring and Enforcement : Procedures for identifying and addressing AI misuse will be established and communicated

units.fit_note: Promises that procedures will be created; does not set steps. Promises that procedures will be established; gives no steps.

units.passage: Resolved, That the Instructor may impose appropriate academic sanctions per the guidelines outlined in the Faculty Senate document for addressing academic misconduct.
units.why: The Senate says the 'Instructor may impose appropriate academic sanctions per the guidelines', stating who sanctions but naming no specific penalty.
units.fit_note: Gives the instructor authority to sanction under existing Faculty Senate guidelines but states no concrete penalty (A had filed it under P37).

units.passage: Faculty & Staff – Violations of this policy will be handled in accordance with the university’s normal disciplinary processes for faculty and staff

The sentence describes what the university will do, so actor is admin and modality informs.

units.passage: Inform students that academic misuse of AI will be directed to the Office of Community Standards.
units.why: 'academic misuse of AI will be directed to the Office of Community Standards' sets the referral route for misuse, a formal reporting procedure (P81).
units.fit_note: Names the office misuse goes to; procedural steps are not given.

units.passage: To uphold academic integrity, we emphasize following the established processes and guidelines outlined in the university's code of conduct. This ensures a fair and consistent approach to addressing concerns
units.why: 'following the established processes and guidelines outlined in the university's code of conduct' routes concerns to the formal integrity process, so P81.
units.fit_note: Routes suspected AI misuse to the code of conduct without calling it misconduct outright.

units.passage: If you have concerns that a student may be utilizing a Chrome extension, please contact the HCC to inquire about the potential use in your class.

units.fit_note: An inquiry to the Honor Code Council, not a formal report. An informal inquiry to the HCC, not a formal report.

units.passage: a suspected academic integrity violation requiring referral through the Office of Student Conduct
units.why: Instructors decide whether it is an unmet assignment requirement or 'a suspected academic integrity violation requiring referral through the Office of Student Conduct': formal procedure, P81.

units.passage: If, after our conversation, I conclude it’s more likely than not that you did not personally complete an assignment you submitted under your name, I may report a violation to the campus Office of Academic Integrity & Student Conduct.
units.why: 'I may report a violation to the campus Office of Academic Integrity & Student Conduct' is the instructor's option to use the formal reporting route after a conversation. It follows the formal integrity-reporting procedure (P81), not P36 (classifying as misconduct). Instructor, when-misuse, may.

units.passage: We will investigate suspected uses of generative AI that do not follow these guidelines and apply sanctions as outlined in the University of Illinois Student Code.
units.why: "We will investigate suspected uses of generative AI ... and apply sanctions as outlined in the University of Illinois Student Code" states the procedure for suspected misuse, nearest P81 (formal procedure).

units.passage: enforcement must follow the procedures outlined in Article VI of the student code

units.passage: Depending on the strength of the suspicion, options include: Issuing a warning Reporting to the respective honor council

units.fit_note: Also gives issuing a warning as an alternative to reporting.

units.passage: All suspected deliberate violations of academic integrity (plagiarism, fabrication, collusion, or cheating) must be reported to the Center for Student Conduct within two weeks of discovery.
units.why: 'All suspected deliberate violations of academic integrity (plagiarism, fabrication, collusion, or cheating) must be reported to the Center for Student Conduct within two weeks of discovery' sets the reporting duty that applies to AI cheating. P81 fits because it is a required reporting step with a deadline.

units.passage: Faculty may recommend a sanction, however, the Coordinator of Academic Integrity or designee or the Academic Integrity Council will make the final sanction determination.
units.why: 'Faculty may recommend a sanction, however, the Coordinator of Academic Integrity or designee or the Academic Integrity Council will make the final sanction determination' leaves sanctions to the deciding body. P81 fits as a procedural step.

units.passage: using such tools will be considered a violation of Penn’s Code of Academic Integrity. - UPenn Center for Teaching and Learning When AI is Generally Prohibited Use of ChatGPT (or other similar tools or software that generate suggested text) is not allowed in this class for any part of a graded assignment, including generation of ideas, writing of text, or rewriting your own work. Doing so is considered a violation of the cheating and plagiarism standards of the UVM Code of Academic Integrity. Violations could result in failure of the assignment or failure of the course and a notation on your transcript. - UVM Center for Student Conduct [This course] assumes that all work submitted by students will be generated by the students themselves, working individually or in groups. Students should not have another person/entity do the writing of any substantive portion of an assignment for them, which includes hiring a person or a company to write assignments and using artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT. - UMass Amherst Center for Teaching and Learning You are not allowed to use ChatGPT (or tools like it) for your work for this class. Using such tools will be considered a violation of Penn’s Code of Academic Integrity and suspected use will be reported to the Center for Community Standards & Accountability.
units.why: 'suspected use will be reported to the Center for Community Standards & Accountability' states reporting of suspected use. P81 fits.
units.fit_note: Sample from another university; also bans ChatGPT outright.

units.passage: Any suspected violation of the Honor Code should be reported promptly, in writing, to the Office of Undergraduate Academic Integrity.
